findings.where: Screens 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10, their read sentences (the read-through and the Book)
findings.what: guide.mjs puts each SHOW step's read in place of its words (d.read || d.text), and these reads only describe the picture, so a read-through never says momentum is mass × velocity (screen 2), never gives the cause, equal and opposite pushes for the same time (screen 4), and never says where the lost kinetic energy goes (screen 6); start each read with the screen's key sentence, e.g. screen 4: "In the hit, the two balls push on each other equally hard, in opposite directions, for the same time. So the cue ball's arrow shrinks to nothing as the struck ball's grows to the same length. The total stays 0.4 kg m/s forward."

findings.where: Screen 1 (What does the cue ball do?), the task
findings.what: The task says "ideal bouncy" before any screen explains that it means no kinetic energy is lost, yet the Why rests on "An ideal bouncy hit keeps both", so add "so no kinetic energy is lost in the bounce" to the question.

findings.where: Screen 1, the opening picture at 360 px
findings.what: The first thing he sees is two bare balls on the cloth, with no cue, aim line or arrow to hint at the shot, so a dashed path from the cue ball to the struck ball would make the opening look alive.

findings.where: Screen 6 (Energy is not kept), the act line
findings.what: "Slide the bounce from ideal bouncy to sticky" runs the wrong way, because the slider opens at Sticky, so say "Slide the bounce up towards ideal bouncy".

findings.where: Screen 8 (Light into heavy), the act line
findings.what: The heavy-ball switch opens already on, so "Flip the heavy-ball switch and play a shot" takes him to two equal balls, away from the case the words describe, so say "Flip the heavy-ball switch off and on, and play a shot each way".

The words elastic and inelastic, which exam questions use, appear only in the explanation and never on a screen, so name them once on screen 6: "A hit that keeps all its kinetic energy is elastic. One that loses some is inelastic."

findings.where: Screen 13 (Which cannot happen?), the on-screen task
findings.what: Unlike every other puzzle, the task on screen ("Which of these can never happen?") leaves the set-up to the table and picture, so show the read's full question: a 0.2 kg cue ball at 2.0 m/s hits an equal still ball dead centre.

2.0 m/s is also the 30 t wagon's own speed before the hit, so "You divided by the 20 t wagon alone" may misread a learner who thought nothing changed, and a hint such as "Coupled, they move as one 50 t. Divide the total momentum by 50 000 kg." covers both.

findings.where: Every demonstration at 360 px, the Speeds and parts tables
findings.what: When the After cells fill ("3.6 m/s right", "0.17 − 0.17 = 0") they wrap onto more lines than the "–" they replace, so the slider and buttons below jump down as each shot ends, and the rows' height should be reserved from the start.

findings.where: Screen 6 at 360 px, the "After the hit" rows of the nose-to-tail panel
findings.what: The after lanes are packed tighter than the before lanes, so "+0.72" and "total +1.2 kg m/s" nearly touch, and they need the same spacing as "Before the hit".
In dark mode the cue ball is drawn dark with a light ring, so it reads as a black ball rather than the white cue ball, and it should stay light in both themes.
There are four footnote markers, [^2] twice, and the closing bold line repeats [^2], so drop that repeat.
